findings.reason: pushMessage puts the new message into loadedMessages and then calls syncCursorsFromFlat/syncCanLoadFlags. The new message becomes `$newest`, the exists-query finds nothing after it, and canLoadNewer is set to false. Lowered from X1's high to medium: jumpToMessage is only reachable through the 'open-attachment' listener, which nothing dispatches (see C6).
findings.claim: After jumpToMessage loads an older window, a sent or received message is appended right after it. The messages in between are skipped, and canLoadNewer becomes false, so they can never be loaded.
findings.evidence: `pushMessage` does `$this->loadedMessages->put($groupKey, ...->push($message))` and then `syncCursorsFromFlat($flat)` / `syncCanLoadFlags()`. The new message becomes `$newest`, so the `canLoadNewer` exists-query finds nothing after it. After `jumpToMessage` loads messages 2–22 of 30, `sendLike`/`sendMessage`/`appendNewMessage` pushes message 31, and 23–30 are silently dropped from the view. Rated medium because nothing in the views dispatches 'open-attachment' yet (see the separate finding).

findings.reason: message-body.blade.php:16 has a literal `class="..."` and line 17 has `@class([...])`, which emits a second `class` attribute. Lines 27–28 repeat the pattern. HTML parsers keep only the first attribute, so the unread bold/colour classes never apply. The test passes only because it searches the raw HTML string.
findings.claim: Duplicate class attributes drop the conditional unread font weight and colour on the preview and timestamp.
findings.evidence: The paragraph already has a literal class attribute on line 16, then @class emits another class attribute containing the conditional unread styles. The timestamp repeats this pattern on lines 27–28. HTML parsing retains the first attribute, so the conditional styles are discarded.

findings.reason: x-init sets `initializing = false` after 220ms. onAnyMediaLoad only calls scrollToBottom `if (this.initializing)`. The diff removes waitForMedia(), which used to wait for every img/video load or error before revealing.
findings.claim: The wait for media before pinning to the bottom was replaced by a fixed 220ms window, so media that loads later leaves the user scrolled above the latest message.
findings.evidence: x-init calls `scrollToBottom()` after 100ms and sets `initializing = false` after 220ms. `onAnyMediaLoad()` only re-scrolls to the bottom `if (this.initializing)`. The removed `waitForMedia()` resolved on every img/video load or error before `scrollToBottom(); booting = false;`.

findings.reason: scrollToMessageCenter (diff ~174) sets `container.scrollTop = target` without updating lastScrollTop. The resulting onScroll sees delta > 8 and clears jumpTargetId/jumpLockUntil, so onAnyMediaLoad's re-center branch can't run. Only reachable through jumps, which have no UI trigger yet (C6).
findings.claim: A jump scroll cancels its own media re-centering lock.
findings.evidence: scrollToMessageCenterWithRetry() sets jumpTargetId and a 1200ms lock, then scrollToMessageCenter() assigns container.scrollTop without updating lastScrollTop. The resulting scroll event enters onScroll(); any movement over eight pixels clears jumpTargetId and jumpLockUntil. onAnyMediaLoad() therefore cannot recenter that target when media subsequently changes the layout.

findings.reason: chats.blade.php:46 calls `document.addEventListener('livewire:navigated', ...)` inside x-init with no cleanup, and the diff removes `x-persist="chats"` from both page views, so x-init runs again on each navigation. Lowered to low: the stale closures do redundant scroll retries against a detached container, which is a leak and a performance cost rather than a visible defect.
findings.claim: With x-persist removed, every wire:navigate adds another document-level 'livewire:navigated' listener that is never removed.
findings.evidence: `document.addEventListener('livewire:navigated', () => { setTimeout(() => scrollToConversation(), 400); });` sits inside x-init with no cleanup. The diff removes `x-persist="chats"` from pages/chat.blade.php and pages/chats.blade.php, which had kept this element and its init alive across navigations.

findings.reason: Grepping src/ and resources/ finds 'open-attachment' only at Chat.php:110 in getListeners(). No view or JS dispatches it.
findings.claim: Nothing dispatches the 'open-attachment' listener, so jump-to-message cannot be reached from the UI.
findings.evidence: A grep for 'open-attachment' across src/ and resources/ finds only `'open-attachment' => 'jumpToMessage'` in getListeners(); no view or JS dispatches it.

findings.reason: The diff adds `public int $chunk = 10` and the cursor/flag properties without #[Locked], while $totalMessageCount has it. `take($this->chunk)` lets a client fetch the whole conversation in one request. Queries stay scoped to $this->conversation->messages(), so this is a hardening point only.
findings.claim: The paging state (chunk, cursors, flags) is public and not #[Locked], so a client can change it.
findings.evidence: `public int $chunk = 10;`, `public ?string $olderCreatedAt`, `public ?int $olderId`, `public bool $canLoadOlder` and the others have no #[Locked], while the existing `$totalMessageCount` does. `->take($this->chunk)` is used in loadOlder, loadNewer, loadLatestWindow and jumpToMessage. Queries stay scoped to `$this->conversation->messages()`, so no other user's data is exposed.

findings.reason: The messages migration (2024_11_01_000004 line 37) uses `$table->timestamps()`, which has precision 0, so created_at holds no sub-seconds. toDateTimeString() and the Carbon value therefore compare equal under the package schema.
findings.claim: Cursors at whole-second precision may skip or repeat messages when created_at has sub-second precision.
findings.evidence: `$this->olderCreatedAt = $oldest->created_at->toDateTimeString();` is then used in `where('created_at', '=', $this->olderCreatedAt)->where('id', '<', $this->olderId)`, but `syncCanLoadFlags` uses `$oldest->created_at` directly.
